thread:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: runtime canary group CPU and tail latency spike detected for deploy/2026-03-17-smallwave (p95 > 2.5s) — alert: https://alerts.redwood.example/ALRT-9021
oncall-ryan: grabbing this, paging in #eng-oncall. taking primary.
eng-alia: I see increased kernel fallback rates on canary hosts (kernel_v2 -> fallback_v1). Also batching window shrank to 8ms, throughput dropped ~30%.
sre-jin: confirmed. logs show `kv_cache_miss_rate` up and OOM throttles on 3/12 canaries. stack traces pinned to `attention_kernel_v2`.
oncall-ryan: any rolling config changes in the last deploy?
deploy-bot: deploy/2026-03-17-smallwave started 1768889500, 25% traffic to canaries, feature flags: prefetch=true, kernel=v2.
eng-alia: kernel v2 was the main change. We pushed a compiled kernel variant for perf but might be triggering prefetch fanout.
support-liz: Customer ops reporting elevated 5xx for enterprise accounts in us-west-2 ~ 0.9% -> 3%. Major customer #ACME seeing timeouts.
oncall-ryan: labeling P1. Paging SRE rotation. Jin, can you get a quick mitigation?
sre-jin: on it. short-term options: 1) flip kernel flag back to v1 for canaries 2) reduce canary traffic to 0% 3) enable kill-switch that disables prefetch.
oncall-ryan: do 2 + 1 in parallel. reduce traffic to 0 first. I want to minimize customer impact while we investigate.
deploy-bot: reducing traffic to canary group -> stepping to 0% (cmd: `deployctl traffic set --group smallwave --pct 0`)
eng-alia: initiating kernel revert for canaries: `configtool set runtime.kernel=kernel_v1 --targets=canary-smallwave`
sre-jin: also flipping prefetch kill-switch for smallwave: `featurectl off prefetch_smallwave` (will propagate in ~30s).
support-liz: ACME support: sending brief note -> "We've detected a runtime regression in a small canary deploy and are reverting changes; your traffic unaffected within 10-20m."
eng-alia: kernel revert confirmed on all canaries, stats starting to normalize. p95 dropping to ~420ms (was 2.8s).
sre-jin: prefetch off confirmed. kv_cache_miss_rate trending back down. no more OOM events in last 2 min.
oncall-ryan: good. keep monitoring for 15m. Jin please start an MTR and gather: kernel logs, batch window histograms, evictions, and compile artifacts for v2.
sre-jin: will collect and upload to /incidents/1768889999/artifacts. starting trace capture now.
eng-alia: root cause hypothesis: kernel_v2 introduced a codepath that increases transient memory pressure during cold KV accesses which triggers fallback and shrinks batching windows; exacerbated by prefetch fanout. Need deeper profiling.
support-liz: no new customer escalations after traffic reduction, ACME replied "thanks for the quick fix".
oncall-ryan: preparing handoff to oncall queue after stabilization. target: postmortem tomorrow EOD. who owns follow-up?
eng-alia: I'll own the kernel investigation and PR to revert approach. Jin and I will pair on a perf test.
sre-jin: I'll own the mitigation checklist and MTR notes.
incidents-bot: INCIDENT P1 acknowledged at 1768889999, status: mitigated -> traffic reverted, kill-switch flipped. Next steps: postmortem, rollout freeze for kernel_v2, add canary memory pressure test.
oncall-ryan: closing the live paging. leaving thread open for artifact uploads. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
